The polyethylene sheeting Is then removed, the hole excavated, and the
spoil loaded into skips for subsequent wefghing and grading, if required. Care
is needed in the excavation to ensure that the density ring ts not disturbed
and, to this end, the edge of the excavation should be kept at least /50 mm
away from the Inner edge of the ring. The sides of the hole should be
trimmed to minimize projecting stones.

Polyethylene sheeting Is then placed over the ring and hole and partially
secured with sandbags. Water Is then run in from a imeasured source and, at
the same time, the polyethylene lining is fed into the hole, helping It into
crevices and minimizing folds. This continues until the water level fs again up
to the mark on the Inside of the density ring. The difference In the two
volumes is then a measure of the volume of the hole. it is customary to allow
the water to remain In the hole for a period of time to see whether there is
any fall of water level, which would tndicate leaks in the polyethylene lining.

The accuracy of the results of this test can be enhanced by attention to
the following details -

ta) The hole should be made as large as possible.

(bh) The sides of the hole should be made as smooth as
possible.

(c) As thin a gauge of polyethylene as possible should be
used, consistent with ft not fracturing too easily. Two
sheets of 0.4 mm polyethylene laid together have been
found to be satisfactory. It is not quite so flexible as
one sheet of the same thickness, but Is less prone to
punctures.

Accounts of the practical use of this method can be found elsewhere
